summary: 考古学家用游团、部落、酋邦和早期国家比较社会形态。人口、生计、聚落和权力组织有助于区分它们，但这些类别只是理解制度变化的工具。
logic: 早期国家的城市及分类的局限

paragraphs.brief: 当研究学者，包括考古学家和人类学家，研究过去或现在的社会时，建立一个用来测试其思想的排名制度可能非常有用。
sentences: When research scholars, including archaeologists and anthropologists, study societies past or present, it can be very useful to have a system of ranking against which to test their ideas.
当研究学者，包括考古学家和人类学家，研究过去或现在的社会时，建立一个用来测试其思想的排名制度可能非常有用。
A four-fold categorizing system was developed by the American anthropologist Elman Service; each grouping is associated with certain types of site and settlement.
美国人类学家Elman Service开发了一个四重分类系统；每种分类都与某些类型的场地和定居点有关。
The four types are known as bands, tribes, chiefdoms and early states.
这四种类型被称为部落、部落、酋长领地和早期州。

paragraphs.brief: 大多数古石器时代 (超过12,000年前) 的遗址似乎与这种类型的团体有关。
sentences: These are small-scale societies, generally of fewer than 100 people, who live by hunting and gathering, moving seasonally to take advantage of wild (undomesticated) food sources.
这些是小规模的社会，一般不到100人，他们靠狩猎和采集为生，季节性地流动，以利用野生(非家用)食物来源。
Most groups who live in this way today, such as the Hadza of Tanzania or the San of southern Africa, would be classified as bands.
今天以这种方式生活的多数群体，如坦桑尼亚的哈德扎人或南部非洲的桑人，将被归类为部落。
The members of one band are generally related to each other, either by descent or by marriage.
一个部落的成员通常因血统或婚姻而相互关联。
Bands lack formal leaders, so there are no clear economic differences or other differences in status among the members.
部落缺乏正式的领导人，因此，成员之间没有明显的经济差异或其他地位差异。

Because bands are composed of mobile groups, their sites consist mainly of seasonally occupied camps and some other sites, such as work sites, where tools are made or other specific activities are carried out.
由于部落由流动团体组成，其营地主要由季节性占用的营地和其他一些地点组成，如制造工具或开展其他具体活动的工地。
Archaeological sites associated with this type of society may show evidence of insubstantial dwellings, along with the debris of residential occupation.
与这类社会有关的考古遗址可能显示出无实质意义的住房以及居住区占地的残块。
Most sites from the Palaeolithic period (more than 12,000 years ago) seem to be associated with groups of this type.
大多数古石器时代 (超过12,000年前) 的遗址似乎与这种类型的团体有关。

paragraphs.brief: 后者可能由像欧洲多瑙河谷第一批农民那样的独立房屋组成，或者他们的房屋可以组合在一起，如美国西南部的Bueblos，或现在土耳其的Catalhoyuk早期农村。
sentences: These are generally larger than bands but rarely number more than a few thousand people, whose diet is mainly based on plants or domestic animals.
这些食物通常大于带子，但很少超过几千人，他们的饮食主要依靠植物或家畜。
Typically, these people are settled farmers, but for some groups life is nomadic, with a mobile economy based on herds of animals.
这些人通常是定居的农民，但对某些群体来说，生活是游牧的，流动经济以牲畜群为基础。
Although some tribes have officials, these lack the economic base necessary for effective use of power.
虽然一些部落有官员，但缺乏有效使用权力所必需的经济基础。
The typical settlement pattern for tribes is one of permanent agricultural homesteads or villages.
部落的典型定居模式是永久性农庄或村庄。
Characteristically, no one settlement dominates any of the others in the region.
典型地说，该区域没有任何一个定居点控制着任何其他定居点。
Instead, the archaeologist often finds evidence of isolated, permanently occupied houses, or permanent villages.
相反，考古学家往往发现孤立、永久占用房屋或永久性村庄的证据。

These latter may be made up of a collection of free-standing houses like those of the first farmers of the Danube Valley in Europe, or their houses may be grouped together, as in the pueblos of the American Southwest, or the early farming village of Catalhoyuk in what is now Turkey.
后者可能由像欧洲多瑙河谷第一批农民那样的独立房屋组成，或者他们的房屋可以组合在一起，如美国西南部的Bueblos，或现在土耳其的Catalhoyuk早期农村。

paragraphs.brief: 这些原则是按人与人之间在社会地位上的差别排序的原则运作的。
sentences: These operate on the principle of ranking—differences in social status between people.
这些原则是按人与人之间在社会地位上的差别排序的原则运作的。
Different lineages (groups claiming descent from a common ancestor) are graded on a scale of prestige, and the senior lineage, and hence the society as a whole, is governed by a chief.
不同的血统(声称从共同祖先世袭的族群)按声望划分等级，而高级血统，乃至整个社会则由酋长管理。
Prestige and rank are determined by how closely related one is to the chief, and there is no true stratification into classes.
功绩和级别取决于与酋长的关系，没有真正的等级分级。
The role of the chief is crucial.
主任的作用至关重要。

paragraphs.brief: 通常，当地专门从事手工艺品，如陶器、布料和皮革制品，这些和食品的任何剩余部分定期付给主管。
sentences: Often, there is local specialisation in craft products such as pottery, cloth and leatherware, and any surplus of these and of foodstuffs is periodically paid to the chief.
通常，当地专门从事手工艺品，如陶器、布料和皮革制品，这些和食品的任何剩余部分定期付给主管。
He uses these to pay his retainers and may also redistribute them to his subjects as rewards.
他用这些来支付他的聘金并且可以重新分配给自己的对象作为报酬
The chiefdom generally has a centre of power, often with temples, residences of the chief and his retainers, and craft specialists.
酋长领地通常有一个权力中心，往往有寺庙、酋长及其保留者的住所和工艺专家。
Chiefdoms vary greatly in size, but the range is generally between 5,000 and 20,000 persons.
酋长领地面积差别很大，但范围一般在5,000至20,000人之间。

Chiefdoms give indications that some sites were more important than others and may have operated as permanent ritual and ceremonial centres, although they were not centres with an established bureaucracy.
酋长领地表明，有些地点比其他地点更重要，可能作为永久仪式和礼仪中心运作，尽管它们不是常设的官僚主义中心。
Examples are Moundville in Alabama, USA, or the late-Neolithic monuments of Wessex in southern Britain, including the famous ceremonial centre of Stonehenge.
美国阿拉巴马州的摩恩德维尔或英国南部韦塞克斯的新石器时期后期纪念碑，包括著名的斯通亨格仪式中心。

paragraphs.brief: 这些保留着酋长领地的许多特征，但统治者，也许是国王或女王，有明确的权力制定法律并通过常设军队执行这些法律。
sentences: These preserve many of the features of chiefdoms, but the ruler, perhaps a king or queen, has explicit authority to establish laws and to enforce them by means of a standing army.
这些保留着酋长领地的许多特征，但统治者，也许是国王或女王，有明确的权力制定法律并通过常设军队执行这些法律。
The society no longer depends on kin relationships but is stratified into different classes.
社会不再依赖亲属关系，而是被分为不同的阶层。
Agricultural workers and the poorer urban dwellers make up the base of the pyramid, with the craft specialists above them and the priests and relatives of the ruler higher still.
农业工人和较贫穷的城市居民构成金字塔的底部，手工艺专家高于他们，统治者的祭司和亲属仍高于他们。
The society is regarded as a territory owned by the ruling lineage and populated by tenants who have the obligation to pay taxes.
社会被视为由统治家族拥有的领土，由有义务纳税的房客居住。
The central capital houses the officials of a bureaucratic administration.
中央首府是官僚行政当局的官员。
One of their main functions is to collect revenue (often in the form of taxes and tolls) and distribute it to government, army and craft specialists.
其主要职能之一是征收收入(通常以税收和收费的形式)，并将其分配给政府、军队和工艺专家。
Many early states developed complex redistribution systems to support these essential services.
许多早期国家制定了复杂的再分配制度，以支持这些基本服务。

paragraphs.brief: 早期国家社会呈现出一种典型的定居模式，城市在其中发挥着主导作用。
sentences: Early-state societies show a characteristic settlement pattern in which cities play the predominant part.
早期国家社会呈现出一种典型的定居模式，城市在其中发挥着主导作用。

The city is typically a large population centre of more than 5,000 people, with major public buildings, and often there is a pronounced settlement hierarchy with the capital city as the major centre and subsidiary or regional centres as well as local villages.
这座城市通常是一个拥有5000多人的人口中心，拥有主要的公共建筑，并且经常有一个明显的定居层次，首都作为主要中心和子公司或区域中心以及当地村庄。

paragraphs.brief: 当然，过分强调上述四类社会的重要性，或花太多时间就某一类社会是否应被归入一类或另一类，是错误的。
sentences: Certainly, it would be wrong to over-emphasise the importance of the four types of society given above, or to spend too long agonising as to whether a particular society should be classified in one category or another.
当然，过分强调上述四类社会的重要性，或花太多时间就某一类社会是否应被归入一类或另一类，是错误的。
However, in seeking to talk about early societies, we must use words and hence concepts to do so.
然而，在寻求谈论早期社会时，我们必须使用文字，从而使用概念来这样做。
Elman Service’s categories provide us with a good framework to organise our thoughts.
Elman Service的分类为我们提供了一个组织思想的良好框架。

They should not, however, deflect us from focusing on changes over time in the different institutions of a society, whether in the social sphere, the organisation of the food quest, technology, contact and exchange, or the spiritual life.
然而，它们不应使我们偏离对社会不同体制随时间变化的关注，无论是在社会领域、组织食物寻求、技术、接触和交流，还是精神生活。

items.en: There is usually little difference in wealth between the various members of a band.
items.zh: 部落成员之间的财富差别通常很小。
items.why: 游群没有正式首领，成员之间也没有明显的经济或地位差异，因此财富通常相差不大。

items.en: In tribes, farmers typically grow a wide range of food plants.
items.zh: 在部落中，农民通常种植广泛的粮食植物。
items.why: 部落人口的饮食以植物或家畜为主，文章没有列出种植了多少种食用作物。

items.en: A typical tribe has one settlement which is more important than others.
items.zh: 一个典型的部落有一个比其他部落更重要的定居点。
items.why: 典型部落没有任何一个聚落支配本地区其他聚落，排除了题干所说的一处最重要。

items.en: In a chiefdom, social status usually depends on the amount of land a person owns.
items.zh: 在酋长领地，社会地位通常取决于一个人拥有的土地数量。
items.why: 酋邦的威望和等级取决于与酋长的血缘亲疏，文章没有把土地数量作为标准。

items.en: A chiefdom typically contains some workers who are engaged in making goods.
items.zh: 酋长领地通常包括从事商品生产的一些工人。
items.why: 陶器、布匹和皮制品都有专门生产者，说明酋邦中存在从事商品制作的工匠。

items.en: An early state may depend on military power to maintain law and order.
items.zh: 早期国家可能依靠军事力量来维持法律和秩序。
items.why: 早期国家的统治者有正式立法权，并可借助常备军强制执行法律，正对应以军力维护秩序。

items.en: Bureaucratic officials in early states receive higher salaries than any other workers.
items.zh: 早期各州的官僚官员的工资高于任何其他工人。
items.why: 早期国家官员负责征税与分配收入，文中没有给出他们与其他劳动者的工资比较。

items.en: What items do bands produce at work sites?
items.zh: 工作地点的乐队生产什么物品？

items.en: Which way of life, apart from settled farming, may be followed by people in tribes?
items.zh: 除了定居的农耕之外，部落里的人还可能遵循哪种生活方式？
items.why: 与定居农耕相对的生活方式。

items.en: How were houses arranged in the village of Catalhoyuk?
items.why: 卡塔霍裕克村的房屋布局。

items.en: Which items, apart from craft goods, may be given by a chief to members of his chiefdom?
items.zh: 除了手工艺品外，哪些物品可由酋长赠予酋长领地的成员？
items.why: 首领可分配的另一种物品。

items.en: What is usually the maximum number of people living in a society which has a chief?
items.zh: 在一个拥有酋长的社会里，人数最多的人通常有多少？
items.why: 有首领社会的上限人口。

items.en: Apart from less wealthy inhabitants of cities, which group forms the lowest class in an early state?
items.zh: 除了城市中较不富裕的居民之外，哪个群体在早期是最低阶层？
items.why: 除城市贫民外的最底层群体。

groups.label: 简答题
groups.instructionsZh: 根据原文简答。每题最多填两个词，可含数字。

第 4 段 · 第 2 句
points: 部落人口的饮食以植物或家畜为主，文章没有列出种植了多少种食用作物。
clauses: Most groups …, such as the Hadza of Tanzania or the San of southern Africa, would be classified as bands.
“who live in this way today”修饰前面的 groups。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 who 时，回看 groups，再把修饰信息接回主句。
…, their sites consist mainly of seasonally occupied camps and some other sites, such as work sites, where tools are made or other specific activities are carried out.
连接词 because 引出“Because bands are composed of mobile groups”，说明主句的原因关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 because 把这一层关系补进去。
